title: Add prompt-shape drift panel and entropy-weighted log sampler
author: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Motivation: We see recurring small-cost regressions where prompt/response shape drift (token count + role distribution) causes sudden changes in token-level latency and cost profiles. Existing telemetry shows per-route aggregates but does not surface prompt-shape distribution shifts or prioritize logs by information content. This PR adds two complementary pieces: 1) a prompt-shape bucketing + drift dashboard (Prompt Shape Drift and Prompt Entropy Explorer) so SREs and ML engineers can see shape cohorts over time, and 2) an entropy-weighted log sampler that biases sampled logs towards high-information invocations to reduce noise and improve alert triage.

What was changed (summary):
- New bucketing logic that computes a compact 'prompt shape key' (role histogram + token-length quantile) at ingest time and emits a shape_id tag on invocation spans.
- A drift detection job that runs daily and annotates shape cohorts with KL divergence vs baseline, exposed as metrics and dashboard annotations.
- Entropy-weighted sampler that assigns a lightweight entropy score (sampled token ngram surprise + role diversity) and uses a tunable reservoir sampler to increase sampling probability for high-entropy invocations.
- Dashboard panels: Prompt Shape Drift (trend + heatmap), Prompt Entropy Explorer (sparkline + sampled log links), Cohort Alert table with auto-suggested hysteresis.
- Docs and runbook describing how to interpret drift signals and how to tune sampler thresholds.

Design notes:
- The shape key is intentionally compact (16-bit hash) to avoid cardinality explosion; cohort rollups are stored in a daily aggregated counter and backed by a downsampled histogram for long-tail shapes.
- Entropy calculation uses a single-pass prefix model and only considers first 64 tokens to keep CPU cost bounded. The sampler is gated behind a feature flag and configured per-tenant with a 1% default bump for high-entropy traffic.
- To avoid alert noise from expected model updates, the drift job supports a 'release-ignore' window; releases tagged in our Linear workflow will automatically suppress drift alerts for the first 24 hours.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for shape-key generation and entropy scorer (observability/tests/*).
- E2E test that injects synthetic prompt shapes and validates that the drift metric moves and that the sampler selects high-entropy traces in the reservoir.
- Load test: ran a 30m canary on staging with 10k rps and observed <3% CPU overhead on telemetry workers with default sampling window.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag default off. Stage rollout: internal telemetry team -> beta tenants -> all tenants over 2 weeks.
- Dashboard panels added to the 'Invocation Insights' org dashboard; access controlled by dashboard role.

Related work: builds on ENG-742 (invocation fingerprinting) and supplements ENG-8421 (cohorting telemetry).

Checklist:
- [x] Shape key library implemented and unit tested
- [x] Drift job and metrics exporter
- [x] Entropy-weighted sampler with feature flag and per-tenant config
- [x] Dashboard JSON + panel templates
- [x] Documentation and runbook
- [x] Load + e2e validation

Runbook excerpt (short):
- If drift spikes for a given shape cohort, check recent model rollouts or prompt template changes; use the Prompt Entropy Explorer to link sampled logs. If high-entropy invocations coincide with increased cost, consider adding explicit prompt prefix caching rules for that cohort.

feat(sampling): implement entropy-weighted reservoir sampler and config
feat(dashboard): add Prompt Shape Drift and Prompt Entropy Explorer panels
docs(observability): add prompt-shape readme and runbook
test: add unit and e2e tests for shape + sampler
review_conversation: Maya Chen: Nice approach. Please add telemetry on sampler select vs baseline select rate so we can measure sampling bias. Also, how does this interact with per-tenant RBAC?

Sofia Ramirez: Added metrics observability.sampler.selected_count and observability.sampler.baseline_count; sampler honors tenant sampling overrides and follows existing RBAC rules for log access (only stores links to logs, logs are gated).
Liam O'Connor: Concerned about cardinality. How do we avoid shape_id explosion for templated prompts with small changes?

Sofia Ramirez: We quantize token-length into coarse buckets and hash role histograms; added a TTL and aggressive downsampling for shapes with <0.01% daily frequency. Updated code to cap observed shape growth and emit a cardinality metric.
Priya Nair: Unit tests look good. Please ensure the feature flag default is off and add a safety kill switch for the drift alerting job.
Sofia Ramirez: Feature flag default is off; added emergency.disable_prompt_shape_drift boolean and a manual mute endpoint.
release_notes: Adds prompt-shape cohorting and drift dashboards plus an entropy-weighted log sampler (feature-flagged). Enables better triage of cost/latency regressions tied to prompt shape changes.
